batch_rationale: The selected rows are intended to improve the learned row distribution rather than favor any V1 or V2 magnitude. Nine rows directly probe previously observed failure modes or their controls. Several additional rows form condition contrasts for the same molecule, reducing ambiguity between solvent response and structural effects. The remaining selections cover H-bond donors, acceptor-rich esters, ketones, aldehydes, halogenated aromatics, flexible hydrocarbons, and low-similarity molecules. This combination should provide both local residual correction and broader support for retraining, while avoiding overreliance on the extreme observed residuals.
batch_strategy: Use a mixed batch of failure repairs, matched controls, broad condition curves, and low-similarity structural coverage. Prioritize direct contrasts around the anomalous diester, cyano-benzophenone, and aromatic alcohol, then add fixed-loading solvent curves for two novel structures and representative polar, nonpolar, H-bonding, halogenated, and flexible molecules.

choices.reason: Cyano-benzophenone loading control tied to a large observed overprediction; helps separate molecule-specific error from condition effects.
Adds a weaker-eluent cyano-benzophenone point to test whether its large residual persists along solvent conditions.
Cyano-benzophenone at 2/1 provides a solvent-response point near the stronger-eluent end for comparison with observed 10/1 behavior.
Diester at 5/1 tests whether the extreme 50/1 overprediction is localized to weak eluent or reflects a broader structural failure.
Intermediate diester solvent condition helps resolve the transition into the anomalous weak-eluent regime.
Lower-loading 50/1 diester is a direct control for the observed extreme residual and tests loading dependence without changing the weak-eluent condition.
Diester at 20/1 supplies another point before 50/1, separating solvent-response curvature from a single-condition failure.
Aromatic alcohol under matched-family conditions tests whether the large underprediction at 5/1 transfers across solvent strength and loading.
Same aromatic alcohol loading at 10/1 provides a controlled comparison to the observed 5/1 underprediction.
H-bond-donating phenol ether expands polar aromatic coverage at a mid-weak eluent and tests transfer beyond the observed structures.
Small neutral hydrocarbon provides a low-polarity reference under 2/1 conditions for row-distribution coverage.
Difluoro benzaldehyde adds a compact aromatic acceptor with halogen and aldehyde effects at 20/1.
Polar ester provides a low-logP acceptor-rich point at 2/1, complementing the more hydrophobic condition examples.
Flexible unsaturated ester tests steric and conformational effects under very weak eluent where condition transfer may be difficult.
Fluorenone supplies a fused aromatic ketone at pure EA, extending structural coverage at the strong-eluent boundary.
Long-chain aryl ketone probes hydrophobic and flexible-substituent effects at 1/1 without relying on a single observed analog.
H-bond-donating isopropyl phenol tests whether acidic or donor-containing aromatic structures show distinct errors under pure EA.
Halogenated anisole at 50/1 adds weak-eluent aromatic coverage with moderate polarity and high loading amount.
Low-similarity diiodobenzene is a novel, nonpolar halogenated structure for testing extrapolation beyond the observed chemical neighborhood.
Bromo diester adds a polar, multi-acceptor structure at 20/1 and tests whether the diester anomaly generalizes across substitution.
Chloroalkyl benzene provides a low-polarity flexible structure at 20/1 for coverage of steric and hydrophobic effects.
Biphenyl aryl ketone extends hydrophobic aromatic coverage at pure EA and probes a low-polarity carbonyl environment.
Bromoacetophenone gives a compact halogenated ketone at 10/1, useful for separating carbonyl and halogen contributions.
Benzyl acrylate adds a flexible ester and unsaturation at 1/1, complementing the more rigid aromatic carbonyl examples.
Pure-EA difluoro benzaldehyde forms a solvent contrast with the same structure at 20/1, testing transfer across a broad condition range.
Low-similarity fused ketone at 5/1 probes sterically constrained aromatic carbonyl behavior outside the dominant observed neighborhood.
Novel hindered benzaldehyde at pure EA establishes the strong-eluent endpoint of a fixed-loading solvent curve.
The same novel hindered benzaldehyde at 10/1 provides an intermediate point with identical loading and carrier conditions.
The same novel hindered benzaldehyde at 50/1 completes a broad solvent curve and tests weak-eluent extrapolation for a low-similarity structure.
Novel tert-butyl chloromethylbenzene at pure EA begins a fixed-loading curve for a nonpolar, sterically hindered structure.
The 5/1 point for the same hindered chlorinated hydrocarbon tests the local solvent response under unchanged carrier and loading.
The 10/1 point extends the matched solvent curve and helps identify whether model condition response is smooth for low-similarity nonpolar chemistry.

feedback_interpretation: The new measurements show mostly modest residuals but an asymmetric tendency toward overprediction: 22 of 32 V1 residuals and 19 of 32 V2 residuals were positive. A few structure-condition combinations dominate the error, especially the 50/1 diester overprediction, the aromatic alcohol underprediction, and the cyano-benzophenone overprediction. This supports targeted condition and loading controls while retaining broad chemical coverage; it does not justify a universal retention correction or treating prediction spans as calibrated uncertainty.
open_scientific_questions: Does the 50/1 diester error persist at lower loading, or is it specific to the original loading and carrier conditions?
Does cyano-benzophenone show a consistent solvent-ratio response across 2/1, 10/1, and weaker eluents?
Does the aromatic alcohol underprediction persist at matched loading when the PE fraction changes?
Do low-similarity hindered aldehydes and chlorinated hydrocarbons reveal systematic condition-response errors?
Which apparent loading effects remain after controlling loading-solvent volume and carrier solvent?
